title: Natural TTS Synthesis by Conditioning WaveNet on Mel Spectrogram Predictions
layout_note: The encoder runs left to right along the bottom row (Input Text -> Character Embedding -> 3 Conv Layers -> Bidirectional LSTM), turns up into a grey attention box in the middle, the orange decoder (Pre-Net, 2 LSTM layers, two linear projections, 5-conv Post-Net) occupies the middle and top-left, and a real mel spectrogram image at top centre feeds a green WaveNet box that outputs Waveform Samples at top right.
grouping: Colour families, not containers: blue boxes for the encoder, orange for the decoder, light grey for attention, green for the WaveNet vocoder, pale yellow for inputs and outputs (Input Text, Stop Token, Waveform Samples).
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles (medium radius) with dark outlines and pastel fills, two-line centred text; a circled plus for the post-net residual add; an embedded real mel-spectrogram plot with axes. Black orthogonal and diagonal arrows; no shadows.
proposed_highlight: Nothing is singled out as new; components are distinguished by colour family only (blue encoder, orange decoder, green vocoder), and the intermediate mel spectrogram is the one picture in the figure.
lesson: Put the model's key intermediate representation in as a real rendered example (here a mel spectrogram with axes) at the hand-off point between two sub-networks, so the reader sees what flows between them.
notes: venue = arXiv (remembered venue: ICASSP 2018; not printed on the arXiv first page); year = arXiv preprint year. Model name 'Tacotron 2' taken from the caption.

arrangement.units: one unframed flowchart; sub-networks are separated only by fill colour (blue encoder row at the bottom, orange decoder in the middle, green vocoder top right)
arrangement.inputs_as: a pale yellow 'Input Text' box at the bottom-left corner
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; Stop Token and Waveform Samples outputs sit at the right in pale yellow boxes

core.what: a three-tier chain that reads bottom to top: the blue encoder row (Input Text -> Character Embedding -> 3 Conv Layers -> Bidirectional LSTM) along the bottom, the orange decoder row in the middle, and the top row ending in a plotted mel spectrogram that feeds a green WaveNet MoL box and then Waveform Samples

relations.form: each tier runs left to right; the bottom row turns up on the right into attention, the middle row's output loops back left and up to the post-net, and the top row runs right through the spectrogram to the vocoder
a line from the Bidirectional LSTM rises and runs left into a grey Location Sensitive Attention box, which exchanges a pair of up/down arrows with the 2 LSTM Layers box above it
the 2 LSTM Layers output forks into two stacked Linear Projection boxes, one going on to a 'Stop Token' output box, the other to the spectrogram path

the autoregressive feedback is one horizontal line from the upper Linear Projection running left above the decoder row to a junction that drops into the 2 Layer Pre-Net and rises into the Post-Net and the + node - drawn as a wire, not unrolled steps
the two-network split is shown by the mel spectrogram drawn as an actual heat-map plot between the feature-prediction network and the WaveNet vocoder

channels.colour: fill = component: blue encoder blocks, orange decoder blocks, grey attention, green vocoder, pale yellow = external inputs and outputs (Input Text, Stop Token, Waveform Samples) - one meaning
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = modules and I/O alike; a circled plus = residual addition; the intermediate is a plotted spectrogram image
channels.line: solid black arrows only; data flow, feedback and attention exchange all share one style

quality.strengths: the intermediate representation that splits the system in two is drawn as real data - a labelled mel-spectrogram plot sits between the predictor and WaveNet; encoder, decoder, attention and vocoder each have one fill, so the role of every block reads from colour
quality.weaknesses: the reading path zigzags (bottom row right, up, middle row right, back left along a long feedback wire, up, then right again); one horizontal line from the Linear Projection serves the autoregressive feedback to the Pre-Net, the Post-Net input and the residual + node, with a double-headed vertical arrow between Post-Net and Pre-Net that is hard to parse; the recurrence is a wire rather than unrolled steps, so the frame-by-frame generation is not visible

insights.structure: Encoder boxes form a bottom row, the decoder sits in the middle with attention between them, and the vocoder plus output sit top right, so the pipeline snakes up the page in three colour families.
insights.data: Text and outputs are pale yellow labelled boxes, while the predicted mel spectrogram is shown as a real colour spectrogram plot with axis ticks at top centre.
insights.emphasis: Only colour family and position separate parts: blue encoder, orange decoder, green WaveNet, grey attention; there is no bold name or container for what is new.
insights.flow: The bottom row runs left to right, a long line climbs from the BiLSTM to attention, the decoder loop runs Pre-Net -> LSTM -> projections, and a feedback line returns leftward to the Pre-Net and up through the Post-Net and a plus into the spectrogram.
insights.avoid: The decoder feedback and post-net lines share one horizontal rail with arrows in both directions, so the autoregressive loop and the residual path are hard to tell apart, and colours are not keyed anywhere.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
